sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: supervisor ages, permit waits, provisional limits, license classes and endorsements, renewal, military and service exceptions, ID cards and fast track
Confusable pairs from the graduated licensing pages, followed by continuation facts on license classes, endorsements, renewal and the military, service, ID card and fast-track rules; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
A teen permit holder needs a supervisor aged 21 or older and may not use a phone at all while driving, while the classroom rule for a permit is 30 hours finished or the first 15 hours of a concurrent course. [A01]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable supervisor age versus classroom hours; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A02
An adult permit holder's supervisor needs to be only 18 or older, and the adult may test after three months at age 19 or older instead of six. [A02]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable teen versus adult permit rules; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A02
Both the instruction permit and the provisional license run for two years, but the permit counts from the day you apply for it and the provisional license from its application date. [A02]
Why it matters: group GDL stages; confusable permit versus provisional validity.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A02
The provisional night limit runs from midnight to 5 a.m., and a licensed companion only lifts it when that companion is at least 25 years old. [A02]
Why it matters: group provisional limits; confusable companion age of twenty-five versus supervisor age of twenty-one.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A03
The provisional passenger cap is one passenger under 20 for the first six months and three for the second six months, and a parent or guardian riding along lifts either cap. [A03]
Why it matters: group provisional limits; confusable first versus second six months.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Under Vanessa's Law an unlicensed teen waits until 18, while a revoked provisional holder waits until 18 or the end of the withdrawal period, whichever is longer. [A03]
Why it matters: group Vanessa's Law; confusable unlicensed teen versus provisional holder; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A05
A Class D license allows all single-unit vehicles except those with a gross vehicle weight of 26,001 pounds or more, those designed to carry more than 15 people including the driver, and those carrying hazardous materials. [A05]
Why it matters: group license classes; prereq for towing limits.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A05
A Class D holder may drive a farm truck carrying farm products, machinery or supplies within 150 miles of the farm, but only as the farmer, an immediate family member or a farm employee. [A05]
Why it matters: group license classes; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A05
A Class D license also covers authorized emergency vehicles of any weight, motor homes and camping trailers for personal use, mopeds, electric-assist bicycles, neighborhood electric vehicles, autocycles, and motorcycles once endorsed. [A05]
Why it matters: group license classes; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A05
You must carry your license whenever you drive, and its back lists your class, endorsements and restrictions; Minnesota has four license classes. [A05]
Why it matters: group license classes; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A06
A Class D driver may tow a trailer weighing 10,000 pounds or less, or a heavier one only when the vehicle and trailer together weigh 26,000 pounds or less. [A06]
Why it matters: group towing; confusable trailer weight versus combined weight; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A06
Endorsements are required for motorcycles, buses, school buses, double and triple trailers, tank vehicles and hazardous materials; each needs an extra written test, and the bus, school bus and motorcycle endorsements also need a special road test. [A06]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A06
Classes A, B and C are commercial licenses that cover every Class D vehicle plus vehicles specific to each class, and a commercial license obtained before 21 carries restrictions. [A06]
Why it matters: group commercial licenses; scope note commercial detail is outside the Class D test.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A06
Employers and employees may face commercial motor carrier rules for vehicles over 10,000 pounds, package delivery vehicles and vehicles carrying more than eight people including the driver, possibly including a federal medical examiner's certificate. [A06]
Why it matters: group commercial licenses; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A07
A Minnesota license usually expires on your birthday and is renewed every four years once you are 21, renewal requires a vision test, and a lost or damaged license is replaced with a duplicate. [A07]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable renewal versus duplicate.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A07
A name or address change before the license expires requires applying for a duplicate within 30 days, while a lost instruction permit is replaced by renewing the permit. [A07]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable thirty-day duplicate rule versus newcomer deadline.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A07
A Minnesota license holder in active military service need not renew until separation or discharge and must then renew within one year with the license and DD-214 papers; the rule extends to a spouse, domestic partner or dependents under 26 living outside Minnesota. [A07]
Why it matters: group military; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A07
A veteran whose disability is rated 100 percent total and service-connected pays no sales, registration or wheelage taxes on up to two vehicles and no title, license or ID card fees. [A07]
Why it matters: group veterans; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A07
A veteran indicator requires separation from service, at least 181 days of active service with an Honorable or General discharge, and is optional with no effect on VA benefits. [A07]
Why it matters: group veterans; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A08
Peace Corps volunteers and federal foreign service employees with a valid Minnesota license need not renew until their service ends, then must renew within one year. [A08]
Why it matters: group service exceptions; confusable with the military rule.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A08
Applying for any Minnesota license or ID registers a citizen or resident aged 18 to 26 with Selective Service, and for applicants under 18 registration is held until the 18th birthday. [A08]
Why it matters: group Selective Service; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A08
You may hold only one type of Minnesota card, so DVS will not issue an ID card to someone with a valid license or permit unless they sign a downgrade statement giving up driving privileges. [A08]
Why it matters: group ID cards; confusable license versus ID card.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R23 | anchor: A09
Fast track service costs an extra $20, processes the card within three business days with UPS delivery within 10 business days and an adult signature, and is not available for a first license, an enhanced card or an upgrade. [A09]
Why it matters: group fast track; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]
